explanation: Chaucer tied Saint Valentine's Day to birds choosing mates in the 1380s. Charles, Duke of Orléans, wrote valentine poems while a prisoner in England after 1415, long before printed cards.

claims.text: Valentine's Day was linked with romantic love by the late 14th century, long before greeting-card companies existed, so they did not invent it.
In Parlement of Foules, written in the 1380s, Geoffrey Chaucer linked Saint Valentine's Day with birds choosing their mates.
Charles, Duke of Orléans, wrote valentine poems while held prisoner in England after his capture at Agincourt in 1415.
Printed valentine cards spread only from the 19th century onwards.
